with.target: Investigate the unresolved causal question recorded in $ARTIFACTS_DIR/triage.md. Read that assessment first; its confirmed facts are context, while its unknowns are the investigation target.

with.work: Plan the current work item from $ARTIFACTS_DIR/triage.md. Read that assessment first, preserve its verified outcome and constraints, and decide the implementation questions it identified. Read $ARTIFACTS_DIR/intel.md too: what usage data says about this work, or why there is none.

Deliver the work prepared by this run. Read $ARTIFACTS_DIR/triage.md first. When present, plan.md or investigation.md is the detailed work order and must be read in full; triage.md records which path produced it and which source assumptions were corrected. On the direct route, triage.md itself is the verified work order. When triage.md routes this run to continue an open pull request, the work is to finish that pull request.

Apply the dependency update specified in $ARTIFACTS_DIR/upkeep-assessment.md. Read that file in full first — it is the verified work order, and you know nothing about this update beyond it and the repository itself. Follow its update order: use the project's own package manager, change the manifest only as the assessment directs, update the lockfile for the target dependency with it, keep churn minimal, and never downgrade anything unrelated. Fix what the bump breaks, check it with the project's own tests for what changed, and if reality contradicts the assessment (version unavailable, an unlisted peer conflict), stop honestly with green false and the contradiction in your summary rather than improvising a different version. Carry the assessment's chosen mechanism, its blast radius, and the alternative it rejected into your report — the reviewer must be able to judge that trade-off from the pull request. Original request: $INPUTS.target

node.prompt:
Read GitHub issue $INPUTS.issue_number in $INPUTS.repository with
`gh issue view $INPUTS.issue_number --repo $INPUTS.repository --comments`.

Decide whether an engineer should investigate it now. Choose `investigate`
for a bug report or regression with enough detail to look into. Choose
`skip` for questions, feature requests, duplicates, spam, and reports too
thin to act on. Give a one-sentence reason.

Investigate GitHub issue $INPUTS.issue_number in $INPUTS.repository. Read
it with `gh issue view $INPUTS.issue_number --repo $INPUTS.repository --comments`,
then read the code in this checkout to find the likely cause. Do not change
any files and do not write to GitHub; your draft is reviewed first.

Draft a comment for the issue: what you think the cause is, the files and
lines involved, and what would confirm it. Say plainly when you are unsure.

wait.attention:
Draft comment for $INPUTS.repository#$INPUTS.issue_number
(classifier: $classify.output.reason). Approve to post it as written;
reject to drop it.

$investigate.output.comment

node.cancel: The draft was rejected; nothing was posted.

node.bash:
set -euo pipefail
body=$investigate.output.comment
gh issue comment "$INPUTS_ISSUE_NUMBER" --repo "$INPUTS_REPOSITORY" --body "$body"
